_about: Season write-ups (original wording). Facts from Lehigh Valley Wrestling History (lehighvalleywrestlinghistory.com), cross-checked against the Hall CSVs and PA-Wrestling; the site data wins on conflicts.

1950-51.headline: Sixth in the Lehigh Valley League, fourth at District XI
story: Coach Harry Wall's team, with six starters gone from the year before, went 2–8 in the Lehigh Valley League and finished sixth of six. Both wins came against Allentown, 29–18 and 25–19. The closest loss was 22–21 to Nazareth: Northampton won four straight bouts from 127 to 154 to lead 21–14, then lost the last two.
At the District XI tournament at Easton on Feb. 24, 1951, Northampton placed fourth with 8 points.

1951-52.headline: Robert Zimmerman wins the district title at 154
story: With eight starters back, Northampton went 3–6–1 in the Lehigh Valley League and finished fourth of six. The season opened with wins over Nazareth (31–11) and Allentown (43–7) and included a 22–22 tie with Easton. Three losses came by a combined eight points, two of them 19–17 decisions to Nazareth and to Easton.

Northampton sent six wrestlers to the District XI finals on March 1, 1952, and placed fourth with 29 points. Robert Zimmerman won the 154-pound title and then placed second at the Northeast Regional in Wilkes-Barre.

1952-53.headline: Program's first District XI team title; league title shared with Bethlehem
story: Northampton won its first District XI team championship, scoring 50 points at the tournament held in its own gym on Feb. 27–28; Bethlehem was next with 27. Eight Northampton wrestlers reached the finals, and John Lawrence (112), Steve Micio (120), Paul Kulp (138) and Dave Laury (165) won titles. Micio and Laury each reached the Northeast Regional final and lost.

In the Lehigh Valley League, Northampton and Bethlehem tied for first at 9–1. Northampton's only league loss was 29–15 at Bethlehem on Jan. 8. In the rematch at home, Northampton won seven straight bouts on the way to a 30–9 win, its first over Bethlehem in six years.

1953-54.headline: Steve Micio reaches the PIAA final at 127
story: Junior Steve Micio did not lose until the state final. He won the District XI title at 127 with a shutout in the final, then took the Northeast Regional title on March 6 with an 8–3 win over defending champion Joe Cawthern of Shamokin. His 8–4 loss in the PIAA final, his first of the season, made him PIAA state runner-up.

With seven starters graduated, four of them district champions, Northampton went 6–4 in the Lehigh Valley League and placed third; Bethlehem won it at 10–0. Easton won both meetings by two and five points, and Bethlehem took the second meeting 23–19 after Northampton rallied from 13–0 down to lead 19–17. The team placed fourth at districts with 19 points.

1954-55.headline: Steve Micio and Edward Keglovits are the program's first state champions
story: Northampton crowned its first PIAA state champions on March 19, 1955. Steve Micio won at 133 with a 5–4 decision over Bill Milligan of Washington, and Edward Keglovits won at 154 by 3–2. Both had won District XI and Northeast Regional titles. The team finished second in the state standings, the best finish by a District XI team since 1940.

At districts, Northampton placed second with 48 points, three behind Easton, with six finalists and three champions: Micio, Keglovits and Bob Meyers (127). In the league it went 7–3, second to 10–0 Easton. Micio's 10–6 loss to Easton's Nido Collina on Jan. 27 was his first league dual loss in about two and a half years.

1955-56.headline: Bob Meyers is PIAA runner-up at 127; four district champions
story: Bob Meyers finished second at 127 at the PIAA tournament after winning District XI and Northeast Regional titles. Joe Recker (95) and Don Santo (133) also won district and regional titles, and Al Lotti (112) won at districts. Northampton placed second at District XI with 58 points, five behind Allentown, and its three regional champions tied Allentown for the most.
Recker pinned every regular-season opponent, and his run of falls reached 15 at districts before he won his regional final 7–5.

In the Lehigh Valley League, Northampton went 6–4 and tied Easton for second behind 10–0 Allentown. All four losses were by seven points or fewer, three of them after Northampton had led, including 20–19 to Allentown and 20–17 to Easton in the finale.

1956-57.headline: Fred Heffelfinger wins the regional title at 95
story: Northampton opened with a 59–0 win over Southern Lehigh, a school scoring record at the time, and went 9–3 in the Lehigh Valley League, second of seven behind 12–0 Allentown. Both losses to Allentown came after Northampton led: 28–25 at home and 23–17 at the Little Palestra.

Fred Heffelfinger (95) and Leonard Breitfeller (120) won District XI titles, Breitfeller in his third straight district final, and the team placed fourth with 55 points. Heffelfinger went on to win the Northeast Regional title. Joe Recker ran his string of consecutive pins to 23 before losing 5–0 to Charles Snyder, and he was district runner-up at 112.

1957-58.headline: Unbeaten in league duals; district team title lost by two points
story: Northampton went 7–0–2 in the Lehigh Valley League, second to Allentown (8–0–1). The ties were 18–18 with Easton, after trailing 9–0, and 17–17 with Allentown, which ended Allentown's 33-meet winning streak. A 61–0 win over Southern Lehigh set a league scoring record. Hill School won a non-league meet 22–16 on Dec. 7.

At District XI, Northampton had six finalists, the most of any team, and led Bethlehem 61–60 going into the 185-pound final. Bethlehem's Bill Werst won that bout over Charley Kuntzelman on a referee's decision after 3–3 and 5–5 overtime, and Bethlehem took the team title 70–68. Gordon Bartholomew was Northampton's only champion, winning 154 by 3–0 over Nazareth's Bill Kraemer.

1958-59.headline: Outright league title at 9–0 and a 10–1 record
story: Northampton won the Lehigh Valley League outright at 9–0, its first league title since 1952–53, and finished 10–1 overall; the loss was 28–13 to Hill School. The team beat Easton 33–10 at Easton in a meeting of unbeaten teams and edged Allentown 18–15 on Jan. 30, ending Allentown's 41-meet unbeaten streak with five straight middleweight decisions, three by one point. The 23–19 opening win over Bethlehem came while winning only four of 11 bouts.

Northampton also won the Haverford College tournament with five individual champions. At District XI it placed fourth with 39 points; Fred Heffelfinger (120), Mike Gontar (138) and Tom Chuss (165) were runners-up.

1959-60.headline: Pete Guntar and Adolph Ebner win district titles
story: Pete Guntar (145) and heavyweight Adolph Ebner won District XI championships and Fred Heffelfinger was runner-up as Northampton placed fourth with 45 points. Guntar and Ebner both lost Northeast Regional semifinals, 2–1 and 2–0.

Northampton went 9–1–1 in the Lehigh Valley League and placed third behind Bethlehem Liberty (10–0–1), which beat it 27–20 before the holiday break. The team opened with a 54–8 win over Notre Dame, beat Allentown 35–11 with four falls, rallied from 23–5 down to tie Easton 25–25, and came back from 15–0 to beat Dieruff 28–24. It was second at the Washington, N.J., holiday tournament, where Guntar and Larry Suranofsky (103) won titles.

1960-61.headline: Brian Brownmiller wins at 154; 10–2 in the league
story: Northampton went 10–2 in the Lehigh Valley League and finished third. Bethlehem Liberty won the league at 12–0, and Liberty and Easton each beat Northampton 35–13, with the Easton meet deciding second place. Northampton beat Phillipsburg 28–17, Wilson 32–11 and Allen 35–21, and came from 19–9 down to edge Dieruff 25–24 on Ron Gogle's first-period fall.

At District XI the team placed fourth with 26 points and had three finalists. Brian Brownmiller won at 154, and Dave Wall (95) and Dave Micio were runners-up, each losing his final to a Liberty wrestler.

1961-62.headline: Western Division title and three district champions
story: Northampton won the Lehigh Valley League's Western Division with a 7–0 division record. It beat Emmaus 28–18, Dieruff 21–17, Allen 29–17 and Phillipsburg 32–16, Phillipsburg's first loss, and lost to Easton 35–8, Bethlehem Liberty 29–17 and Hill School 27–18. The team also won the Washington, N.J., holiday tournament with four champions: Jack Suranofsky (95), Dave Micio (133), Jeff Cole (154) and Willie Gogel (unlimited).

At District XI, Northampton placed third with 57 points. George Reenock (165), Russ Mikovitch (180) and Gogel won titles, and Micio was runner-up for the second straight year. All three champions reached the Northeast Regional finals at Wilkes College and finished second.

1962-63.headline: Dave Wall is PIAA runner-up at 120; Jim Guntar reaches state semifinals
story: Dave Wall, the coach's son, won District XI and Northeast Regional titles at 120 and finished as PIAA state runner-up, losing a close decision in the final after a one-point semifinal win. Heavyweight Jim Guntar also won district and regional titles, taking the regional final 6–5, then lost in the state semifinals. Both district finals went to overtime against Nazareth wrestlers: Wall beat Glenn Newhard and Guntar beat Chip Arduini.

With three district champions and six other starters graduated, Northampton went 5–2 in the Western Division and finished third; Allen won the division by beating Northampton 27–15 in the final week. The team opened with a 42–5 win over Notre Dame but lost 23–20 to Easton after leading 17–0. It tied for seventh at districts with 34 points.

1963-64.headline: League champion at 8–0 and 13–1 overall
story: Northampton won the Lehigh Valley League title at 8–0, two games ahead of Emmaus, and went 13–1 overall; the only loss was a non-league meet with Phillipsburg. Wins included Allen twice (22–17 after trailing 17–11, and 28–18), Easton 26–21, clinched by Dean Berg's 5–3 decision at 180, Hill School 25–22, and Stroudsburg 32–12 in the meet that clinched the league.

Dave Wall won his second District XI title at 120 and was Northeast Regional runner-up, losing the final 6–5 to Al Goss of West Snyder. Wall and transfer Charlie Nordquist (138) won titles at the Washington, N.J., holiday tournament. The team scored 21 points at districts.

1964-65.headline: Second straight league title and the first league tournament title
story: Northampton went 11–2 overall and 5–0 in the Lehigh Valley League for a second straight league title. It also won the first Lehigh Valley League tournament, held at Northampton, with 107 points and seven champions; Stroudsburg was second with 76. The losses were 31–16 at Easton and 25–17 at Allen, which Northampton had beaten by the same score earlier.

At District XI the team placed second with 46 points to Easton's 59. Jack Hildenbrandt (95) and Charlie Nordquist (138) won titles, Nordquist by pinning Easton's Bob Colletta in the final, and Greg Amore (145) was runner-up. Hildenbrandt and Nordquist both lost in the regional semifinals at Wilkes College.

1965-66.headline: Third straight league title at 6–0; league tournament won again
story: Northampton won its third straight Lehigh Valley League title at 6–0, clinching it with a 40–13 win over Catasauqua in late January. Other league wins included Stroudsburg 32–19, Whitehall 44–9, Slatington 33–14 and Lehighton 38–5. Non-league losses came against Phillipsburg 30–12, Hill School 26–23 and Allen 39–6.

The team won the second Lehigh Valley League tournament on Feb. 12 with four champions: Jack Hildenbrandt (103), Tony Mauser (112), John Toth (127) and John Faryna (154). In December, Mauser ended Stroudsburg's Tom Coco's 21-meet winning streak. Northampton scored 3 points at District XI.

1966-67.headline: League co-champion with Stroudsburg at 5–1
story: Northampton shared the Lehigh Valley League title with Stroudsburg, both 5–1, securing its share with a 21–19 win over Lehighton. Emmaus handed Northampton its league loss, 28–20, on Dec. 22. Other wins came against Stroudsburg 25–20, Bethlehem Catholic 30–23, Whitehall 33–13, Slatington 29–13 and Catasauqua 36–11. Non-league losses included Nazareth 46–5 in the Dec. 2 opener, Wilson 25–20, Hill School 26–20, Allen 47–12 and Hellertown 30–6.

At the league tournament Northampton was second, 68–61 to Stroudsburg, with champions Bill Feichtl (95), Jack Hildenbrandt (103), Tony Mauser (120) and Marlin Coleman (154). The team scored 4 points at District XI.

1967-68.headline: Three-way share of the league title with Emmaus and Stroudsburg
story: Northampton tied Emmaus and Stroudsburg for the Lehigh Valley League title, each at 5–1, extending its run of league titles to five straight seasons. Wins included Wilson 23–20 after trailing 14–3, Lehighton 30–15, Emmaus 26–15 (Emmaus's first loss), Whitehall 33–17, Slatington 37–17, Allentown Central Catholic 52–2 and Catasauqua 29–11. Losses came against Nazareth 23–20, Stroudsburg 38–10, Hellertown 27–11 and Bethlehem Catholic 40–9.
Rick Spengler was unbeaten into February and took his first loss at District XI, 9–2 to unbeaten Keith Ernst of Palisades. Northampton scored 16 points at districts.

1968-69.headline: Second straight three-way league title; 9–5 overall
story: For the second year in a row, Northampton shared the Lehigh Valley League title with Emmaus and Stroudsburg, going 6–1 in the league and 9–5 overall. The league loss was 27–18 to Emmaus. Wins included Catasauqua 40–5 in the Dec. 12 league opener, Wilson 22–20, decided by heavyweight Randy Moats' 7–1 win over Skip Dalrymple, Stroudsburg 25–18, Lehighton 34–6, Whitehall 38–8, Slatington 42–5 and Palmerton 47–3. Hellertown beat Northampton 32–11, its third straight win in the series, and Nazareth won 25–19.
Bill Feichtl, a district runner-up the year before, lost 4–2 in the District XI quarterfinals at 103. The team scored 7 points at districts.

1969-70.headline: Fourth in the league at 4–3, ending a six-year title run
story: Northampton finished fourth in the Lehigh Valley League at 4–3, ending a run of six straight seasons with at least a share of the league title. Catasauqua beat Northampton for the first time, 30–21, on Dec. 18, and a 30–15 loss to Nazareth on Jan. 10 was the team's fourth straight. Wins came over Palmerton 57–0, Stroudsburg 28–15, Whitehall 37–10 and Slatington 49–5; other losses were to Hellertown 33–6, Lehighton 28–18, Emmaus 27–15 and Bethlehem Catholic 26–13.
At the league sectional at Slatington, Northampton placed second with 65 points to Emmaus' 74 and qualified eight wrestlers for districts, where the team scored 21 points.

1970-71.headline: Outright Lehigh Valley League title at 7–0 in Harry Wall's final season
story: Northampton went 7–0 in the Lehigh Valley League and won the title outright, finishing 8–5 overall. A 22–19 win over Emmaus on Feb. 3, after leading 22–11 with two bouts left, clinched at least a share of the title, and a 35–9 win over Whitehall on Feb. 10 made it outright. Other league wins included Lehighton 23–20, Stroudsburg 29–14, Catasauqua 36–12 and Palmerton 53–6.

Ralph McCandless (103), George Hummel (112) and Mike Ziatyk (154) won titles at the Christmas City Tournament, where the team placed second. Northampton also won the league sectional team title with four champions and sent seven wrestlers to districts.
It was Harry Wall's 26th and last season as head coach.

1971-72.headline: Thomas Ortwein takes over; third place in the Lehigh Valley League
story: Harry Wall, Northampton's coach since the program's first season in 1945-46, died before the season. He finished with a 180-110-4 record over 26 seasons. Thomas Ortwein became head coach.

Northampton went 5–2 in the Lehigh Valley League and finished third. League wins came over Whitehall 40–14, Slatington 57–3, Palmerton 46–10, Catasauqua 25–18 and Stroudsburg 39–11. The title-deciding dual against Lehighton on Jan. 22 went to Lehighton after Northampton led 23–18.

1972-73.headline: Third in the league; two Christmas City champions
story: Northampton finished third in the Lehigh Valley League at 5–2, with league wins over Whitehall, Slatington, Palmerton, Lehighton and Stroudsburg. The team placed second at the Christmas City Tournament, where Terry McReil (98) and Jerry Heist (119) won titles, and was runner-up at the league tournament with two champions.
On Jan. 20, Steve Clemons pinned in the final bout for a 27–21 win over Allentown Central Catholic.

1973-74.headline: Second in the league as the PIAA splits into two classes
story: This was the first season PIAA wrestling had two classes, and Northampton wrestled in the large-school bracket at districts. The team finished second in the Lehigh Valley League at 5-1-1 behind Lehighton, which won the deciding dual 25–19. Northampton also tied Catasauqua 28–28.

Steve Clemons' 13–3 heavyweight win decided a 27–26 victory over Wilson, and his third-period pin sealed a 29–25 win over Emmaus. Rick Billy (105) and Don Arndt (138) won titles at the first league holiday tournament, where Northampton placed second. Eight wrestlers advanced from the sectional to districts.

1974-75.headline: Rick Billy wins district and regional titles, PIAA Class AAA runner-up
story: Rick Billy won the District XI title at 105 as the fifth seed, beating the top seed in the semifinals and Henry Callie 2–1 in the final. He beat Callie again for the regional title and finished second at the PIAA Class AAA tournament.

Northampton crowned five champions at the Lehigh Valley League tournament, more than any other team: Billy, Joe Liskanich (112), Rick McCandless (132), Robin Farina (138) and Don Arndt (167). Lehighton won the team title 107.5-104.5.
The team finished third in the league at 5–2. On Jan. 11, Northampton beat Nazareth 23–22, coach Thomas Ortwein's first win over Nazareth in seven tries.

1975-76.headline: Rick Billy repeats as district champion and places fourth at states
story: Rick Billy won the District XI AAA title at 126 in overtime over Bethlehem Catholic's Mike Bold and placed fourth at the PIAA Class AAA tournament, his second straight state medal.

It was Northampton's first season in the new East Penn League after the Lehigh Valley League disbanded. The team went 1–10 in league duals, with the win coming 42–3 over Allentown Central Catholic. Thomas Ortwein coached his fifth and final season.

1976-77.headline: Gordon Bartholomew's first season; Lee Billy district runner-up
story: Gordon Bartholomew succeeded Thomas Ortwein as head coach. Northampton went 3–8 in the East Penn League, tied for ninth, with wins over Whitehall 27–18, Allentown Central Catholic 57–3 and Emmaus 46–9.
Lee Billy reached the District XI AAA final at 105 and finished second.

1977-78.headline: 3–8 in the East Penn League
story: Northampton went 3–8 in the East Penn League and finished in a three-way tie for eighth with Dieruff and Whitehall. The Dec. 8 dual with Whitehall was decided by falls in the last two bouts, giving Whitehall a 27–26 win. It was Gordon Bartholomew's second season as head coach.

1978-79.headline: 6–5 in the league; sophomore Matt Billy district runner-up
story: Northampton went 6–5 in the East Penn League and finished sixth. League wins included Allen 27–22 on Jan. 18 and Freedom 25–24 in February, when Northampton won three of the last four bouts after trailing 21–15.
Sophomore Matt Billy reached the District XI AAA final at 98, beating the second seed 3–1 in the quarterfinals and winning 8–0 in the semifinals before finishing second.

1979-80.headline: 12–4 season with a comeback win over league champion Easton
story: Northampton finished 12–4 overall and 7–4 in the East Penn Conference, tied for fifth. In the league opener, the team trailed Easton 27–14 with four bouts left, won all four and took the dual 29–27. It was Easton's only league loss.

On Jan. 19, Ed Wagner's 4–2 heavyweight decision won a 26–25 dual at Nazareth. Late in January, Northampton came back from 20–17 down with three bouts left to beat Liberty 32–20. Dave Kistler (126) was named outstanding wrestler at the Christmas City Tournament. It was Gordon Bartholomew's last season as coach.

1980-81.headline: Matt and Stephan Billy win district and regional titles
story: Matt Billy (105) and Stephan Billy (98) both won District XI AAA and Northeast Regional titles. Stephan pinned Nazareth's Greg Noll in the district final. Matt went on to place sixth at the PIAA Class AAA tournament.
Roger Washburn took over as head coach, with Jerry Heist as an assistant. Northampton tied for eighth in the East Penn League.

1981-82.headline: 6–13 season in Roger Washburn's second year
story: Northampton finished 6–13 and went 2–9 in the East Penn League, tied for tenth. On Jan. 30, the team led Pocono Mountain 28–0 after six bouts but lost the last six and the dual, 31–28. It was Roger Washburn's second and final season as head coach.

1982-83.headline: Don Rohn takes over; Stephan Billy wins second district title
story: Don Rohn became head coach after five seasons at Hazleton. Northampton went 2–9 in the East Penn League and finished 11th of 12. In late January, Pocono Mountain won the last five bouts to beat Northampton 32–22.
Stephan Billy won the District XI AAA title at 119, his second district championship.

1983-84.headline: Sean Finkbeiner wins Northampton's first PIAA Class AAA state title at 145
story: Sean Finkbeiner won the PIAA Class AAA championship at 145 after taking District XI and Northeast Regional titles. A transfer from Saucon Valley, where he was a two-time state runner-up, he won the title on his third trip to the state tournament. He was also named outstanding wrestler at the Christmas City Tournament.
Northampton went 5–6 in the East Penn Conference and finished seventh. Wayne Reiss clinched a 32–29 win over Emmaus with a fall at 185. All six league losses were by eight points or fewer.

1984-85.headline: 15–2 season; Joe Billy and Wayne Reiss win district titles
story: Northampton went 15–2 in duals and 9–2 in the East Penn League, third place, in Don Rohn's third season. The only losses were to Easton 31–20 and Phillipsburg 41–12. On Jan. 24, the team beat Nazareth 36–24 for its first win over Nazareth in five years.

Wayne Reiss clinched league wins over Liberty, 31–24 after Northampton trailed 10–0, and Allen, 31–29. Joe Billy (126) and Reiss (heavyweight) won District XI AAA titles. Billy was runner-up at the Northeast Regional and placed third at 126 at the PIAA Class AAA tournament. The team was fourth at districts.

1985-86.headline: 15–3 season with three regional champions
story: Northampton won three Northeast Regional titles: Brad Billy (119), Stan Reuben (126) and Jeff Kaboly (167). Billy and Kaboly were also District XI AAA champions. Brad Billy placed fourth and Reuben sixth at the PIAA Class AAA tournament. The team was third at both districts and regionals.

Northampton went 15–3 in duals and 9–2 in the East Penn League, tied with Phillipsburg for second. The team won the Christmas City Tournament and beat Easton 33–20 on Jan. 4 in the new junior high gym.

1986-87.headline: 16–1 and a share of the East Penn League title
story: Northampton went 16–1 in duals and shared the East Penn League title with Easton at 10–1. The only loss was 24–23 to Easton on Jan. 7. League wins included Nazareth 32–15, Liberty 26–15, Parkland 34–11 and Phillipsburg 23–16. A heavyweight major decision broke a 25–25 tie in a 29–25 win over Quakertown.

The team won the Bethlehem School District preseason tournament and the Christmas City Tournament, four champions at each. Northampton placed second at District XI AAA with seven semifinalists. Mike Bartholomew placed third at 132 at the PIAA Class AAA tournament.

1987-88.headline: East Penn League champions and District XI team champions
story: Northampton won the East Penn League title outright and won the District XI AAA team title. Ed Youwakim (119), Kevin Smith (167) and Mike Recker (105) were district champions, and Smith also won a Northeast Regional title. Smith, Recker and Don Suranofsky (112) each placed fourth at the PIAA Class AAA tournament, where the team finished fifth.

1988-89.headline: Share of the league title; Kevin Smith PIAA Class AAA runner-up
story: Northampton shared the East Penn League title with Easton and Phillipsburg and placed second at District XI AAA. Kevin Smith won district and regional titles at 171 and finished second at the PIAA Class AAA tournament. Brian Chamberlain (160) and Don Suranofsky (125) also won district titles, and Mike Laury won a regional title at 130. Chad Billy (103) and Mike Recker (119) placed fourth at states, and the team finished fifth.

1989-90.headline: Outright East Penn title; Rian Youwakim PIAA Class AAA runner-up
story: Northampton won the East Penn League title outright and placed second at District XI AAA. Rian Youwakim finished second at 119 at the PIAA Class AAA tournament, and Chad Billy placed sixth at 112. Mike Laury won district and regional titles at 135.

1990-91.headline: Chad Billy wins the state title at 112; the Kids win the East Penn Conference
story: Chad Billy won the PIAA Class AAA title at 112 pounds, beating Meadville's Jeff Cervone 7–4 in the final. He was the only state champion from the Lehigh Valley that season.

Under coach Don Rohn, Northampton went 21–2 and won the East Penn Conference at 11–0. The Kids won the Christmas City Tournament by half a point, 197–196.5 over Nazareth. In January they beat Easton 21–19 on Jan. 17, and two nights later beat Nazareth 30–26 when heavyweight Jason Grim pinned his man in the final bout to erase a 26–24 deficit. At the Cedar Cliff Duals they lost 32–31 to Shikellamy after leading 21–0.
Nazareth beat Northampton 31–26 in the District XI Duals final and finished ahead of the Kids for the District XI team title. Northampton placed 22nd at the state tournament.

1991-92.headline: A shared East Penn Conference title, three district champions and a state finalist
story: Northampton opened the season ranked No. 1 in Pennsylvania, won its first 19 duals and finished 20–2. A 26–21 loss at Phillipsburg on Feb. 8 was the only conference defeat, and the Kids shared the East Penn Conference title with Easton and Phillipsburg at 10–1. Along the way they beat Easton 31–21 on Jan. 16 and Nazareth 33–25 on Jan. 18.

Nazareth beat the Kids 34–20 in the District XI Duals semifinals. At the District XI tournament, Joe Reuben (125), Steve Gaugler (140) and Andy Doster (160) won titles, and Northampton sent five wrestlers to states from the Northeast Regional, the most of any District XI team. Reuben reached the PIAA Class AAA final at 125 and placed 2nd. The team finished 14th at states.

1992-93.headline: Unbeaten at 24–0, Northampton wins its first PIAA team title
story: Northampton went 24–0, won the East Penn Conference at 11–0 and won its first PIAA Class AAA team championship. Coach Don Rohn was named state Coach of the Year.

The Kids won the Christmas City Tournament with six champions and the Cedar Cliff Duals, then beat Nazareth 26–23 on Jan. 23 at Liberty after trailing 21–7. In the postseason they won the District XI Duals, beating Easton 37–12 in the final, and the District XI team title, 216–194 over Nazareth, with 11 semifinalists. They added the Northeast Regional team title with four champions.
At states Mike Tomsic won the 112-pound title by pinning Conestoga's Jason LaMotta in 45 seconds. Frank Mazzocchi placed 3rd at 119, Steve Gaugler 4th at 152 and Denny Liberto 6th at 103.

1993-94.headline: A second straight 24–0 season and a second PIAA team title
story: Northampton repeated as PIAA Class AAA team champion and finished 24–0 again, winning the East Penn Conference at 11–0. Don Rohn won his 200th dual meet at Northampton in the District XI Duals final, 35–12 over Easton, and was named AAA Coach of the Year.

After graduating eight starters, the Kids won the Christmas City Tournament with 12 of 13 wrestlers placing, won the Cedar Cliff Duals 43–15 over Dallastown in the final and beat Canon-McMillan 45–16. They beat Easton 29–22 on Jan. 26 and Nazareth 22–18 on Feb. 14 at Stabler Arena.

Northampton won the District XI team title by 76 points with five champions; Dave Emili won at 119 from the No. 6 seed and was named Outstanding Wrestler. The Kids also won the Northeast Regional team title. At Hershey, Whitey Chlebove won the 130-pound title, Dave Emili was runner-up at 119, and Denny Liberto and Ryan Gumlock placed 3rd.

1994-95.headline: Third straight PIAA team title in the first Mountain Valley season
story: Northampton won its third straight PIAA Class AAA team championship, led by Denny Liberto's title at 103. Dave Emili was runner-up at 119, Ryan Gumlock and Craig Fenstermaker placed 3rd, Tim Mazzocchi 5th and freshman Christian Luciano 6th.

The Kids went 16–4 and finished 2nd in the new Mountain Valley Conference at 5–1, behind Nazareth. On Dec. 10 they beat Canon-McMillan 31–29 for a 50th straight dual win before Walsh Jesuit ended the streak 28–27 that day. They finished 2nd to Walsh at the Ironman Classic in Ohio, won the holiday tournament at Liberty with seven champions, and won the Cedar Cliff Duals. Nazareth beat them 28–23 on Jan. 20.

Easton edged the Kids 25–24 in the District XI Duals semifinals. Northampton crowned six District XI champions, the most of any team, while placing 2nd in the team race, then won the Northeast Regional team title with five champions.

1995-96.headline: Three regional champions and two state medals
story: After graduating seven starters, Northampton went 13–7 and finished 2nd in the Mountain Valley Conference at 5–1, behind Nazareth, which beat the Kids 34–15 on Jan. 20. Northampton won the Cedar Cliff Duals and placed 6th at the Walsh Ironman, where Rick Umstead won the 189-pound title.

Christian Luciano (152) and Umstead (189) won District XI titles, and the team finished behind Easton and Nazareth. At the Northeast Regional the Kids placed 3rd with 85.5 points and had three champions: Brian Ware (145), Umstead and John Hard (275). Umstead placed 3rd at states and Luciano 4th, and Northampton finished 10th as a team.

1996-97.headline: Mountain Valley champions at 6–0; Luciano reaches the state final
story: Northampton won the Mountain Valley Conference at 6–0 and finished 16–4. The Kids beat Liberty 25–19 on Dec. 14, Phillipsburg 22–19 on Jan. 11 in a dual where eight bouts were decided by three points or fewer, and Nazareth 23–22 on Jan. 18. They won the Cedar Cliff Duals, beating Manheim Central 33–27, and placed 3rd at the Mid Atlantic Classic in Delaware. Easton (49–9) and Parkland (26–17) handed them two of their losses.

In the District XI Duals the Kids beat Liberty 28–24 before losing 50–13 to Nazareth in the semifinals. Freshman Tommy Rohn (119), Christian Luciano (171) and John Hard (275) won District XI titles, and Hard won the Northeast Regional. At states Luciano was runner-up at 171, and Mike Sommer (140) and Hard placed 4th. The team finished 6th.

1997-98.headline: A 21–0 season ends with a fourth PIAA team title
story: Northampton went 21–0, won the Mountain Valley Conference at 6–0 and swept the District XI Duals, District XI, Northeast Regional and PIAA Class AAA team titles. Christian Luciano (171) and John Hard (275) won state titles, Phil Hard placed 3rd at 189 and Seth Lisa 5th at 119.

The Kids won the Cedar Cliff Duals 42–15 over Dallastown in the final and beat Nazareth 38–13 on Jan. 17. Easton tied them 24–24 on Jan. 24, with Northampton winning on criteria, and John Hard's pin in the last bout beat Parkland 33–27. On Jan. 31 Luciano set the school record for falls in a season.

Parkland was the runner-up three times in the postseason: 26–23 in the District XI Duals final, 223.5–203 at the District XI tournament, where the Kids went 6-for-6 in finals, and 94–93 at the Northeast Regional. Don Rohn was named District XI Coach of the Year.

1998-99.headline: District Duals and District XI team titles; a team-duals trip to states
story: Ranked No. 1 in the nation by Amateur Wrestling News and USA Today to start the season, Northampton went 18–4 and tied for 2nd in the expanded 12-team Mountain Valley Conference at 9–2, behind Parkland. The Kids won the Reno Tournament of Champions in Nevada, the Hurricane Classic and the Cedar Cliff Duals, 37–12 over Dallastown in the final. They beat Easton 30–25 on Jan. 16 and lost 26–24 at Phillipsburg two days later.

Northampton won the District XI Duals, beating Bangor 45–15, Easton 26–21 and Parkland 27–23 in the final, which ended Parkland's 20-dual winning streak. In the PIAA Class AAA team duals the Kids lost 44–18 to Gettysburg in the quarterfinals.

The Kids won the District XI team title with repeat champions Seth Lisa (125), Justin Haupt (130) and John Bauer (171), and shared the Northeast Regional team title with Easton. Aaron Suranofsky placed 3rd at 103 at states.

1999-00.headline: Don Rohn's last season brings state tournament and team duals titles
story: In Don Rohn's 18th and final season as head coach, Northampton went 23–1, won the PIAA Class AAA team title with a state-record eight place winners, and won the PIAA team duals for the first time, beating Connellsville 30–19 in the final.

The only loss came against Ohio's St. Edward's, 32–18, at the Easton-Phillipsburg Duals. The Kids won the Bethlehem Holiday Classic and the Cedar Cliff Duals, beat Easton 29–21 on Jan. 22, and won the Mountain Valley Conference with a 34–15 win over Nazareth on Feb. 5.

Northampton won the District XI Duals, the District XI team title with six champions and the Northeast Regional team title. Ryan McCallum won the state title at 130; Jeff Ecklof and Tommy Rohn were runners-up. Coach Don Rohn finished 309–59 in duals at Northampton.

2000-01.headline: Terry Daubert's first season: 18–3 and 3rd at states
story: Terry Daubert took over as head coach after Don Rohn's retirement, and the Kids went 18–3 and finished 2nd in the Mountain Valley Conference at 6–1, behind 7–0 Easton. Easton beat Northampton 38–17 on Jan. 17 and again, 28–21, in the District XI Duals final, and finished ahead of the Kids at the District XI and Northeast Regional tournaments.

Northampton placed 3rd at the Beast of the East with three champions: Aaron Suranofsky (119), Seth Lisa (130) and Phil Hard (189). The Kids were 2nd to Blair Academy at the Bethlehem Holiday Classic with four champions and won the Cedar Cliff Duals, 44–13 over the host in the final.
At states the Kids placed 3rd as a team with three finalists. Jeff Ecklof won the 125-pound title, beating Garnet Valley's Pat O'Brien 12–6. Lisa (130) and Phil Hard (189) were runners-up.

2001-02.headline: Five district champions and a 4th-place state finish
story: Northampton went 19–2 and 6–1 in the Mountain Valley Conference. Both losses came against Easton: 36–15 at Easton on Jan. 26, in a dual between the state's top two ranked AAA teams, and 35–16 in the District XI Duals final. The Kids beat Nazareth 29–16 at Nazareth on Jan. 23. Jeff Ecklof won his 100th career match on Feb. 13 against Whitehall.

The Kids placed 4th at the Beast of the East and 3rd at the Bethlehem Holiday Classic. At the District XI tournament they finished 2nd with five champions: freshman John Paukovits (112), Ecklof (130), Bobby Zuber (145), Josh Haines (171) and Jon Oplinger (189). Ecklof, Haines and Oplinger won Northeast Regional titles.
Northampton placed 4th at states. Oplinger was runner-up at 189, Ecklof and Haines placed 3rd, and Zuber 4th.

2002-03.headline: Four state champions lead Northampton to its sixth PIAA team title
story: Northampton won the PIAA Class AAA team title 98–80.5 over Easton, and four Kids won state championships: Joey Ecklof (135), Jeff Ecklof (145), Josh Haines (189) and Jon Oplinger (215). Jeff Ecklof's title was his second.

The Kids went 21–2 and won the new Lehigh Valley Conference at 7–0. They won the Bethlehem Holiday Classic 232–221.5 over Blair Academy, the Cedar Cliff Duals and the Parkland Duals, and beat Easton 31–29 on Jan. 25 for Terry Daubert's first win over Easton as head coach.
Easton beat the Kids 34–23 in the District XI Duals final and finished ahead of them at the Northeast Regional tournament. Northampton had five District XI champions and four regional champions.

2003-04.headline: Repeat PIAA team champions with ten state place winners
story: Northampton repeated as PIAA Class AAA team champion with 132.5 points to Easton's 83.5 and ten place winners. Joey Ecklof (145), Josh Haines (189) and Jon Oplinger (215) each won a second state title. Terry Daubert was named PIAA Coach of the Year and NHSCA National Coach of the Year.

The Kids went 20–1 and won the Lehigh Valley Conference at 7–0, clinching it with a 31–30 win over Easton. They won the Virginia Duals and the Cedar Cliff Duals, placed 2nd at the Bethlehem Holiday Classic with six champions and 3rd at the Beast of the East. The only loss was 29–25 to Easton in the District XI Duals final.
Northampton won the District XI team title with a record 281 points and six champions, then won the Northeast Regional team title with four champions and 11 state qualifiers.

2004-05.headline: Joey Ecklof wins his third state title at 152
story: Joey Ecklof won his third PIAA Class AAA title, beating Greensburg Salem's Donnie Jones 10–3 in the 152-pound final.

After graduating two state champions, the Kids tied for 4th in the Lehigh Valley Conference. They hosted and won the first Cement Town Duals on Dec. 11, beating Milton 60–8 and Cumberland Valley 37–27, and placed 3rd at the Bethlehem Holiday Classic. Whitehall beat Northampton 31–30 on criteria on Jan. 12, its first win over the Kids in 22 years. Easton (28–20) and Nazareth (31–24) also won league duals, and Nazareth beat the Kids again, 25–24, in the District XI Duals semifinals.

Northampton finished 2nd at the District XI tournament with 233 points and three champions: Steve Mytych (125), who was named Outstanding Wrestler, John Paukovits (140) and Ecklof. Ecklof, Mytych and Justin Wieller (215) won Northeast Regional titles. The team placed 15th at states.

2005-06.headline: Cedar Cliff Duals champions; Justin Wieller medals at 189
story: Northampton won the Cedar Cliff Duals on Jan. 7, beating Warren County (Va.) 72–0, Red Lion 52–10 and Mount St. Joseph (Md.) 49–12 in the final. The Kids also beat Council Rock South 29–26 at the Konkrete Duals and Freedom 51–13 at the District XI Duals. Their recorded losses came against Cumberland Valley (32–24), Caesar Rodney of Delaware (30–29) and Nazareth (37–15). Justin Wieller won the District XI and Northeast Regional titles at 189 and placed 5th at states. The team finished 3rd at both the District XI and Northeast Regional tournaments.

2006-07.headline: Justin Wieller wins the state title at 215 for a young team
story: Justin Wieller won the PIAA Class AAA title at 215 pounds, beating Manheim Central's Jordan Enck 6–4 in the final. Mike Wechsler (152) placed 5th, Marcus Wilson (171) 6th and Jimmy Sheptock (140) 7th, and Northampton finished 8th as a team.

After graduating five starters, the Kids had six sophomores and a freshman in the lineup early in the season. They won the Cedar Cliff Duals 4–0, beating the host 50–18 in the final, went unbeaten at the NHSCA Festival at Pleasant Valley, and placed 3rd at the Bethlehem Holiday Classic. Easton (36–19 on Jan. 3) and Nazareth (33–21) won league duals, and the Kids tied for 3rd in the Lehigh Valley Conference.

Easton beat Northampton 34–21 in the District XI Duals semifinals. The Kids placed 3rd at the District XI tournament, where Wilson won at 171 with his 100th career win, and 3rd at the Northeast Regional, where Wieller won the 215-pound title.
